title: overrun
body:
Buffer overruns can occur when a program erroneously writes more data to a buffer than it can hold, potentially overwriting adjacent memory. This can lead to various types of errors such as crashes, data corruption, or security vulnerabilities, including unauthorized access or control over a system.

**Receiver overrun**, the I/O sense, is a different failure with the same name, and it is
the one [[Programmed I-O]] and [[Polling]] run into. The device puts a byte in the
[[Data Register]] and sets the ready flag; before the [[CPU]] gets round to reading it, the
next byte arrives and overwrites it. The first byte is simply gone, and the
[[Status Register]] raises an overrun error bit to say so.

Nothing is written out of bounds here: the data is *lost*, not spilled into adjacent
memory. Same word, opposite direction.

The fixes are the rest of the course. [[Buffering]] widens the window,
[[Interrupt Driven I-O]] removes the polling delay, and [[Direct Memory Access]] takes the
CPU out of the path entirely.
